title: Detroit Man Exchanges Gunfire With Federal Agents During Escape Attempt
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Detroit, Michigan — On November 14, 2025, officers with the Detroit Police Department, working alongside the Michigan State Police and agents from the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives, moved into a residential area on the city’s east side to take a suspect into custody. Investigators believe the suspect was connected to a non-fatal shooting and more than a dozen incidents involving gunfire into homes, vehicles, and neighborhoods over the previous week. When officers moved in, the man fled by car, crashing through lawns and sidewalks and striking a house before authorities disengaged ground units and relied on aerial tracking to limit risk to the public.

The pursuit continued into Livernois Avenue, where police say the suspect attempted multiple crimes, including an attempted carjacking at a gas station and a second carjacking that triggered an exchange of gunfire with federal agents. After fleeing again, state troopers ultimately stopped the vehicle with a tactical maneuver, prompting the suspect to run while still armed. Officers repeatedly ordered him to drop the weapon, and shots were fired as he advanced toward police. The suspect was taken into custody and given medical aid at the scene, and a handgun was recovered. The man was taken to an area hospital, where he is currently in critical condition. Federal prosecutors have since indicted 33-year-old Terrance Markyce Davis, on charges including carjacking, assaulting and attempting to murder ATF Special Agents. Authorities say both criminal proceedings and an internal review of the incident are ongoing.
